LastReply.Name: Blanchefleur
LastReply.Text: It was a gift, but I do not remember from whom. I do remember a sailor that came to visit me the other day. He said it looked like something they have a tale about over in Abel. Something involving Fiosachd. But it sounded too much like a silly big city legend, and he was such a bad storyteller...Besides, he brought no gifts from the outside world.

Dialog.Name: Blanchefleur
Dialog.Text: Yes, I just told you that. But that is all there is to it. Just to let you know, sometimes my friend Aundy comes from the temple she lives in, in Abel, and tells me stories fo the big city. I asked her about that, out of curiosity, and she did not know anything. If Fiosachd has any ties to this pretty cap of mine, and not even his Acolyte knows it, who would, other than himself? Oh well...You are an Aisling, free to travel across the world. Maybe you can find a way to ask the patron of Rogues himself.

Dialog.Name: Keefe
Dialog.Text: Hello.  What can I do for you?

Dialog.Name: Keefe
Dialog.Text: What kind of answers?

Dialog.Name: Keefe
Dialog.Text: You address your questions to a god directly? What got into your mind, Aisling? The doubt-solving god is Luathas, not me.

Choices.Text: So you will not tell me of the cap?

Dialog.Name: Keefe
Dialog.Text: Tell you? That is not my problem. I make sure what is supposed to remain hidden, remains. Sometimes I am a bit late, but I can always take it back and hide it somewhere else. I am the God of Chance, things usually work out for me, one way or the other. But I am saying too much. Leave Aisling, I have no further business with you.

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: Hello.  What can I do for you?

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: Hello.  What can I do for you?

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: Hello.  What can I do for you?

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: You have come far in your search, have you not? But more awaits ahead of you.

Choices.Text: I am eager to continue, I wish to help the boy.
More!? But I have been to all corners of Temuair already!

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: Yes, the boy in Abel. I am surprised you still remember he was the first step of this endless walk. Helping the boy is the largest of the tasks.

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: There are many others.

Choices.Text: What will I gain in the end?

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: You must first track your prize's origins. You are close. The tortuous path that you seek lies in damp marshes beyond these mountains. Look for information there, but remember, as Deoch has great goodness behind his dark figure, important information may be hidden behind what seems ignorant.

Dialog.Name: Logan
Dialog.Text: My role in your epic pursuit is done. Go now, may the Light of Danaan guide you.
